notes: Sprites sourced from spritedatabase.net (HeartGold/SoulSilver overworld rip, credited on-sheet to ripper 'Grim').

Each source block has 8 32x32 columns: 0-1 = front/down walk (2 poses), 2-3 = back/up walk (2 poses), 4-5 = one side-facing pose (2 frames), 6-7 = the same pose mirrored horizontally (confirmed 100% pixel-identical to an hflip of columns 4-5 for all 12 species).

CORRECTION (verified by inspecting the delivered pixels for all 12 species): an earlier reading of this rip described columns 0-3 as a four-frame front walk and concluded the source had no back-facing art. That is wrong. Columns 2-3 are the BACK view -- no face, tail/spines visible. Playing columns 0,1,2,3 as one cycle makes a walker flip between facing the camera and facing away every other frame.
Left/right facing was determined by visual inspection (Bulbasaur's snout points left in column 4, right in column 6) and applied uniformly.

The delivered PNGs are a 4x4 grid whose rows are down/left/right/up, but the 'up' row is a byte copy of the 'down' row. The real back-facing frames therefore sit at columns 2-3 of that row, which is what directions.up.frames points at. Read `directions.<dir>.frames` as the column sequence to play in row `rowOrder.indexOf(dir)`; do not assume a row's four columns are one cycle.
Transparency was produced by flood-filling each frame's background from its four corners (the source uses a soft cyan vignette per cell, not a single flat color), not a fixed color-key.
